headline: Sensex and Nifty decline on persistent FII selling, high oil prices, and global yield pressure.

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: FII selling and elevated crude oil prices exerted severe pressure on equity benchmark indices.
High bond yields in the US market kept global investor sentiment cautious.
High derivatives market activity caused significant volatility and sharp swings in Indian equities.
Concerns over global monetary policy and rate hikes contributed to market declines.
whatHappening: Indian stock markets closed lower with Sensex and Nifty facing extended losses in September.
Goldman Sachs and BNP Paribas divested over 68 lakh BSE shares worth Rs 2,186 crore.
Tata Chemicals dropped by 4.5% amidst broader market weakness.
Allcargo Logistics announced the appointment of Vijay Nehra as Managing Director & CEO.
summary:
Indian benchmark indices traded lower following persistent foreign institutional investor selling and elevated crude oil prices.
Global bond yields remaining near multi-decade highs and heavy derivatives trading added to the market volatility.
Key stock updates included institutional stake divestment in BSE and Tata Chemicals declining 4.5%.
